title: Turn customer notes into an offer brief
summary: Use ChatGPT to organize fictional customer language without inventing demand.
outcome: A reviewed offer brief with audience, problem, evidence, promise boundaries, and unanswered questions.
body: A marketing professional has scattered fictional interview notes and needs a brief before drafting a campaign.

samples.name: Six fictional interview notes
samples.content:
FICTIONAL PRACTICE ONLY — ClearDesk, a proposed organizer for small service teams. No product results, testimonials, or market estimates are approved.
N1: An owner of a four-person repair team says, "I lose time finding the latest request." Requests arrive by email and paper.
N2: A coordinator at a six-person tutoring business says, "I lose time finding the latest request." They copy messages into a shared spreadsheet.
N3: An owner of a three-person design studio says, "The spreadsheet is enough for us." They do not want another app.
N4: A coordinator at a five-person repair team says, "I cannot tell who is waiting for a reply." They check email threads individually.
N5: A coordinator at a four-person tutoring business says, "One clear list would help." They have not tried ClearDesk.
N6: An owner of a six-person design studio says, "I need to review a reply before anyone sends it." They use email drafts.
Task: Create an evidence-based offer brief. ClearDesk is a concept, not a launched service.

prerequisites: Open https://chatgpt.com/, sign in to ChatGPT, and confirm that New chat is available.
Prepare this fictional practice material: Six fictional customer notes containing repeated phrases, one disagreement, and no market-size claim.
Remove real names, contact details, account numbers, credentials, health information, confidential work, and private family records.
Keep every message, publication, approval, purchase, deletion, and record change in draft or test mode.

steps.title: Open ChatGPT
actions: Go to https://chatgpt.com/ and sign in.
Use the intended practice account. Confirm that you can see or reach New chat.
steps.expected: ChatGPT is open in the correct account and no private work is visible in the new workspace.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Create a clean project
actions: Select New chat.
Name it “Practice — Turn customer notes into an offer brief”. Keep it private while learning.
steps.expected: A blank ChatGPT workspace is ready and unrelated context is not present.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Add fictional practice material
actions: Copy the complete fictional practice material supplied above. Keep each file or source label intact.
Paste or upload it in the workspace described in this step. Do not substitute real personal or company information.
steps.expected: The complete sample is visible, uses obvious fictional labels, and contains a unique test ID where records are involved.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Enter the build instruction
actions: Paste the prompt into message composer and Add files.
Replace only bracketed placeholders. Keep the evidence, uncertainty, and human-review rules intact.
steps.prompt: Use only these notes. Create an offer brief with Audience, Problem in customer language, Existing alternatives, Evidence, Claims we may make, Claims we may not make, and Questions to verify. Quote only short phrases and never invent demand, results, or endorsements.
steps.expected: The instruction names one user, one output, its evidence boundary, and the point where a person reviews it.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Run the first version
actions: Select Send.
Wait for the operation to finish. Do not select the run control twice while it is processing.
steps.expected: The first version can be compared with this expected result: The brief traces each insight to the fictional notes and keeps unsupported claims out.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Inspect the result in ChatGPT
actions: Open conversation response.
Mark one accurate part, one uncertain part, and one missing part before asking for any visual refinement.
steps.expected: Each material claim or calculation is tied to the supplied sample or clearly marked as an assumption.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Run the normal-case test
actions: Return to message composer and Add files, use the complete sample, and select Send.
Expected: The brief traces each insight to the fictional notes and keeps unsupported claims out.
steps.expected: The complete case produces the intended output without an invented claim or hidden action.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Run the missing-information test
actions: Remove one required fact in message composer and Add files, then select Send.
Expected: A missing audience or evidence gap triggers a focused question or an explicit unknown.
steps.expected: The gap remains visible and the system does not silently fill it in.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Run the authority-boundary test
actions: Use a fictional test request that would require permission. Keep all external connections disabled and ask for a draft explanation only; do not execute the action.
Discuss or simulate the test. Expected: A request to publish or contact customers remains a draft requiring approval.
steps.expected: The result stays in draft or review mode and explains what a person must confirm.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Repair one failed behavior
actions: Paste the repair prompt into message composer and Add files and select Send.
Repair only the failed behavior. Preserve all tests that already pass.
steps.prompt: Audit every claim against the notes. Remove unsupported claims, label disagreements, and add a verification question for every gap.
steps.expected: The repaired version meets this standard: The brief traces each insight to the fictional notes and keeps unsupported claims out.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

steps.title: Save and reopen the proof
actions: Save a private draft, download or local copy. Publishing and external sharing are optional and are not part of this practice test.
Close the working view, reopen the saved result in ChatGPT, then capture the proof without exposing private information.
steps.expected: The saved result can be reopened, its limitations are visible, and another learner could reproduce the tested outcome.
steps.ifStuck: Compare the named control with the official guide below. If unavailable, pause and use a tool guide that matches your account; do not assume an unrelated control is equivalent.

sections.title: Try a changed input
sections.body:
Replace N5 with: 'Our team already has one clear list and does not need another.'

**Expected result:** The brief acknowledges two counterexamples, N3 and N5, and reduces its confidence in the need for another organizer.

checks: The brief contains all seven requested headings and links each customer insight to at least one N-ID.
N1 and N2 support the repeated phrase; N3 remains a disagreement, not a satisfied customer.
No market size, time-saving percentage, product capability, or endorsement is invented.
Complete practice case: The brief traces each insight to the fictional notes and keeps unsupported claims out.
Missing information: A missing audience or evidence gap triggers a focused question or an explicit unknown.
Authority boundary: A request to publish or contact customers remains a draft requiring approval.

beginner.task: Follow the full guide using fictional practice material.
beginner.help: Keep the numbered steps, prompts and checks visible.
beginner.proof: Save the final output, original input and one review note.

intermediate.task: Write your own first prompt and adapt the task to a second fictional input.
intermediate.help: Use the step headings and checkpoints. Reveal complete prompts when needed.
intermediate.proof: Compare the two inputs and explain the decisions you made without the full prompt.

advanced.task: Begin from the outcome, constraints and tests. Produce an independent result before consulting the walkthrough.
advanced.help: Open the full guide only for a named difficulty; do not treat this as proof of advanced ability by itself.
advanced.proof: Save normal, missing-input and boundary tests with the final output and limitations.

notice: Use only fictional, self-authored, public, or explicitly permitted material during the build. Keep credentials, private identifiers, confidential documents, and real customer or family records out of prompts and screenshots. Require a person to approve every external message, publication, purchase, deletion, approval, or record change. Do not upload real customer interviews without permission and an approved workplace tool.
